walkthroughs.body_html:
Use of Biological Resources — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Use of Biological Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Use of Biological Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Bacteria can be used to make human insulin because they have been:
options: genetically modified with the human insulin gene
fed pure human insulin
selectively bred for many generations
heated to change their proteins

mcqs.q: In bread-making, yeast makes dough rise by producing:
options: carbon dioxide
oxygen
lactic acid
ethanol gas only

mcqs.q: Selective breeding increases a desired feature by:
options: breeding individuals that show that feature over many generations
inserting new genes in a laboratory
raising the temperature of the eggs
feeding the animals more protein

mcqs.q: Raising CO2 levels in a glasshouse increases crop yield because it:
options: increases the rate of photosynthesis
kills all the pests present
provides nitrogen for the plants
lowers the temperature of the air

mcqs.q: How are bacteria able to make human insulin?
options: The human insulin gene is inserted into the bacteria's DNA (genetic modification), so they transcribe and translate it to make insulin.
Selective breeding only works on plants, never animals.
Bacteria are fed human insulin and then release it again.
Bacteria naturally produce human insulin in their own bodies.

mcqs.q: What gas makes bread dough rise?
options: Selective breeding only works on plants, never animals.
Bread rises only because oven heat turns water to steam.
Yeast respires anaerobically and produces carbon dioxide, which forms bubbles that make the dough rise.
Bread rises because yeast produces oxygen.

mcqs.q: Does selective breeding change DNA the way genetic modification does?
options: No - selective breeding chooses existing parents over generations; it does not directly insert genes from another species.
Bacteria are fed human insulin and then release it again.
Selective breeding means adding new genes into an organism in a lab.
Selective breeding only works on plants, never animals.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Micropropagation”?
options: Rearing fish in controlled conditions, managing water quality, food supply, predators and disease in order to maximise the yield of fish.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.
Producing many genetically identical plants from small pieces of tissue grown on nutrient agar under sterile conditions.
Growing crops in enclosed conditions where temperature, light, carbon dioxide and watering are controlled to raise photosynthesis and yield.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fish farming”?
options: Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.
Growing crops in enclosed conditions where temperature, light, carbon dioxide and watering are controlled to raise photosynthesis and yield.
Rearing fish in controlled conditions, managing water quality, food supply, predators and disease in order to maximise the yield of fish.
Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together over many generations so that those features become stronger in offspring.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Selective breeding”?
options: Rearing fish in controlled conditions, managing water quality, food supply, predators and disease in order to maximise the yield of fish.
Growing crops in enclosed conditions where temperature, light, carbon dioxide and watering are controlled to raise photosynthesis and yield.
Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together over many generations so that those features become stronger in offspring.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glasshouse production”?
options: Growing crops in enclosed conditions where temperature, light, carbon dioxide and watering are controlled to raise photosynthesis and yield.
Rearing fish in controlled conditions, managing water quality, food supply, predators and disease in order to maximise the yield of fish.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.
Transferring a gene from one organism into another to give a useful characteristic, such as inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Yeast fermentation”?
options: Transferring a gene from one organism into another to give a useful characteristic, such as inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria.
Growing crops in enclosed conditions where temperature, light, carbon dioxide and watering are controlled to raise photosynthesis and yield.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.
Producing many genetically identical plants from small pieces of tissue grown on nutrient agar under sterile conditions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Genetic modification”?
options: Anaerobic respiration in yeast that converts sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide, used in brewing and in bread-making.
Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together over many generations so that those features become stronger in offspring.
Rearing fish in controlled conditions, managing water quality, food supply, predators and disease in order to maximise the yield of fish.
Transferring a gene from one organism into another to give a useful characteristic, such as inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria.

sequence.def: Select individuals with the desired characteristic
Pick offspring showing the trait most strongly
Cross the best offspring with each other
Trait reliably appears throughout the population
